title: Hybrid Cache Coordinator — Design Spec & Rollout Plan
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
=======

This design spec describes the Hybrid Cache Coordinator (HCC), a cross-service component that unifies prefix/KV caching across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. HCC's objective is to improve tail latency and per-token cost by coordinating cache placement, eviction, and prefilling policies across the serving runtime and the orchestration layer. This document includes goals, non-goals, architecture, config surface, rollout plan, SLO impact analysis, test plan, and ownership.

Why HCC now
------------
- Increasing model sequence lengths and multi-turn chat workloads have amplified KV-cache miss amplification across concurrent replicas.
- Existing per-node caches lead to duplicate state and higher memory pressure in dedicated pools.
- Workloads exhibit skew (hot prompts, heavy tenants) where coordinated caching yields material cost and latency improvements.

Goals
-----
1. Reduce median and 95th percentile token latency for chat workloads by coordinating cache warmup and eviction across replicas.
2. Reduce aggregate memory footprint for KV prefixes across a dedicated pool by >= 20% for skewed workloads.
3. Expose a small operator and API surface to allow per-tenant and per-route cache policy overrides.
4. Be deployable in-hosted, dedicated, and Private (VPC) modes with identical control-plane APIs; implementation details can vary by deployment mode.

Non-goals
---------
- Not a global state store for arbitrary application state. HCC will only manage inference-related cache metadata and prefetch assets (prefixes, quantized KV blobs).
- Not intended to replace LRU per-node caches entirely on first rollout; we will phase in coordination gradually.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
1. Control plane service (HCC-controller): maintains cache policy, global prefix popularity map, and prefill schedules. Runs in the Redwood control plane for hosted; for Private deployments it runs as an optional customer-managed control-plane service (process-mode).
2. Local agent (hcc-agent): lightweight per-node daemon that implements local eviction actions, receives prefill tasks, and reports telemetry. Runs colocated with serving runtime.
3. Prefill store: object store (S3/GCS/MinIO) or shared filesystem used to stage precomputed KV blobs (quantized). Not required for basic coordination but recommended for large-scale warmups.
4. Runtime integration: RPCs between hcc-agent and serving runtime to apply KV blobs to in-memory/kernelsafe stores and to adjust batch scheduling priorities.

Sequence diagram (text)
-----------------------
1. Runtime observes repeated prefixes for route R. 
2. Runtime reports aggregated prefix fingerprints to hcc-agent.
3. hcc-agent forwards compacted events to HCC-controller (batched).
4. Controller updates popularity map and, if threshold crossed, schedules prefill task to agent(s).
5. Agent prefetches prefabs from prefill store or requests runtime to generate.
6. Prefilled KV is pinned with TTL on nodes chosen by the coordinator.
7. Controller monitors hit-rate; evicts or reassigns when popularity decays.

Control API (summary)
--------------------
- GET /v1/policies
- POST /v1/policies {route: string, tenant_id: string, policy: {pin_ttl_s: int, replication: int, priority: enum}}
- POST /v1/prefill-requests {route, tenant, fingerprint, target_nodes: [id], source: auto|manual}
- GET /v1/metrics/{route}

Configuration matrix (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| Parameter | Default (hosted) | Notes |
|-----------|------------------|-------|
| sampling_window_s | 60 | Aggregation window for prefix counts |
| popularity_threshold | 150 | Count of occurrences in window to consider prefill |
| default_replication | 2 | Number of nodes to pin prefills for redundancy |
| pin_ttl_s | 900 | Time to keep a prefetched prefix before eligible for eviction |
| max_prefill_bytes_per_node | 40MB | Soft limit to prevent memory starvation |
| prefer_same-pool | true | Prefetch nodes co-located with request-serving pipelines |

(Represented above as a preformatted table in Confluence UI.)

Eviction and safety policies
---------------------------
- Eviction priority: 1) expired TTL 2) lowest access recency across pool 3) explicit controller-triggered reassign.
- Safety: Agents will not evict pinned prefixes below a minimum_reserved_bytes (default 8MB) without controller approval.
- Backpressure: If node memory becomes constrained, agent signals overload and controller reduces replication targets and deprioritizes low-priority prefills.

Compatibility and fallback behavior
----------------------------------
- If HCC-controller is unreachable, agents continue local policies (existing LRU) and mark coordination degraded.
- For Private deployments without a central prefill store, agents may coordinate via direct peer-to-peer transfers initiated by controller instructions.

SLO and metric impact analysis
-----------------------------
Primary metrics (to emit):
- prefix_hit_rate (per-route, per-tenant)
- prefill_success_rate
- average_prefill_latency_ms
- memory_reserved_bytes
- eviction_count
- coordination_health: enum {ok,degraded,offline}

SLO targets (proposal):
- prefix_hit_rate: baseline +10% improvement within 30d for top-20 routes after rollout.
- coordination_health: >= 99.5% ok for hosted clusters.

Telemetry schema (example)
------------------------
- timestamp: ISO8601
- node_id: string
- route: string
- fingerprint: string
- access_count: int
- last_access_ms: int
- action: enum {reported,prefill,evict,fail}

Security and tenant isolation
-----------------------------
- All control-plane RPCs are authenticated using mTLS and token-based ACLs.
- Prefilled artifacts stored in prefill store must be encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private deployments that request it.
- Access control: policies allow scoping by tenant_id and route; controller will enforce authorization on manual prefill and policy updates.

Operational runbook (summary)
----------------------------
1. Detect coordination degraded: alert if coordination_health != ok for > 5 minutes.
2. Quick remediation: restart local hcc-agent. If persisted, failover controller to standby.
3. Emergency mitigation: set default_replication=1 and increase popularity_threshold by 2x to reduce prefill churn.
4. Post-incident: collect agent and controller traces (/var/log/hcc/*) and increase sampling to capture misses for 24h.

Rollout plan (phased)
---------------------
Phase 0 — Canary (2% of hosted traffic; 1 dedicated pool)
- Deploy hcc-controller canary and hcc-agent to a small pool.
- Run in passive reporting mode (no prefill actions) for 7 days.
- Validate metrics plumbing and telemetry.

Phase 1 — Coordinated prefill (10% traffic)
- Enable auto-prefill for low-risk routes (non-sensitive, synthetic test prompts).
- Limit default_replication=1 and max_prefill_bytes_per_node=8MB.
- Run for 14 days; compare prefix_hit_rate and tail latency.

Phase 2 — Pool-wide rollouts (50% traffic)
- Increase replication to default 2, expand route coverage to top 50 routes.
- Enable memory-based backpressure.

Phase 3 — Global rollout
- Full rollout across hosted pools, optional opt-in for Dedicated customers, and private packaging for Private deployments.

Migration steps for Dedicated customers
--------------------------------------
1. Preflight: run the hcc-scan tool to estimate expected prefill storage and memory overhead.
2. Agree on replication and pin_ttl defaults with customer.
3. Schedule maintenance window for initial rollout (prefer low-traffic hours).
4. Start in passive mode; after 7 days enable low-risk prefill.

Testing and validation plan
--------------------------
- Unit tests for controller decision logic (popularity thresholding, reassignment).
- Integration tests: simulate skewed prefix traffic and verify replication, eviction behavior, and failover.
- Load tests: measure memory footprint reduction and tail latency under synthetic chat workloads.
- Upgrade tests: agent upgrade must be rollbackable without losing pinned KV blobs.

Metrics dashboard and alerts (recommended)
----------------------------------------
- HCC Overview: coordination_health, total_prefills, prefill_success_rate, prefix_hit_rate (global).
- Node panel: per-node memory_reserved_bytes, eviction_count, local_hit_rate.
- Alerts: coordination_health != ok (P1), prefill_success_rate < 90% for 10m (P2), memory_reserved_bytes > 90% of node capacity (P1).

Backward compatibility and versioning
-----------------------------------
- HCC API will use semantic versioning: v1 for initial release. Agents will support negotiation of controller API version during bootstrap.
- Controller will accept both v1 and v1beta clients with clear deprecation timelines (>=3 months notice).

Open implementation decisions (to be resolved in follow-up design doc)
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Global vs per-pool popularity accounting: sketch above biases toward pool-local popularity for performance; final decision requires cost analysis.
- Prefill artifact format and compression: need to choose a canonical blob format (protobuf vs flatbuffers) that balances deserialization latency and storage size.

Appendices
---------
A. Example prefill request (JSON)
{
  "route": "chat.default",
  "tenant_id": "acct_123",
  "fingerprint": "fp:abcd1234",
  "target_nodes": ["node-12", "node-15"],
  "source": "auto"
}

B. Expected rollout checklist
1. Merge controller and agent feature flags behind `hcc_enabled` remote feature flag.
2. Complete telemetry contract and dashboard templates.
3. Run 2-week canary and collect SLA delta report.
4. Prepare customer-facing docs and Private deployment packaging.

C. Related reading
- KV cache management (runtime-wiki)
- Serving batching and prefix handling design doc

Notes
-----
This spec is intended to be an implementable blueprint for the next 6–9 months. Detailed implementation PRDs (storage format, RPC schemas, and PB formats) will be published as follow-ups and linked from the related_pages list.
